name: After § 54
title: REPORT on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the European Union for the financial year 2024, Section I – European Parliament
part_text: 54 a. Furthermore, in the context of the democratic process, expresses concern that certain major parties and candidates were excluded from the Eurovision debate organised by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) at Parliament in the run-up to the European elections and thus with its financial support; recalls the concerns set out in the OSCE report regarding the impact “on the overall integrity of the elections, particularly when accompanied by limited public participation in the political debate,” the fact that “in some countries, senior officials have used their official positions to promote their parties,” as was the case with the then-French Prime Minister, and “However, participation in this debate was limited to the Spitzenkandidaten nominated by the existing political groups within the current European Parliament. Such an approach prevented four political parties from participating and is not in accordance with paragraph 7.8 of the 1990 OSCE Copenhagen Document"; recalls the prohibition on financing European political parties with Parliament’s budget intended for the promotion of Parliament, thereby constituting a financial advantage for the parties that is prohibited by Regulation 1141/2014 and should be subject to financial sanctions by the APPF; deplores the persistent discrimination by European institutions against elected officials on the basis of their political affiliation, and that Parliament, a place of democracy by its very nature, contributes to financing this knowingly and in violation of the rules;
